body.prompt: A refrigerator door in a small Korean apartment kitchen at night, covered with many paper delivery menus held by magnets. In the foreground a hand holds a smartphone; the paper menus peel off the fridge and stream into the phone screen like a ribbon of tiny flying sheets.

Spring 2020 on a narrow Korean shopping street. A row of small restaurant owners in aprons and face masks stand in front of their shops, arms crossed, tired and upset. Above them float several smartphone outlines each showing a single small star. Delivery scooters parked at the curb.

A fried chicken delivery paper bag on a wooden table, cut open in cross-section like a cutaway diagram and divided into vertical slices of very different widths. The widest slice holds raw chicken, cooking oil bottles and packaging; another slice holds a smartphone and a delivery scooter; a medium slice holds a small government building; the thinnest slice holds a tiny shop owner holding a few coins. Viewed from slightly above.

Bird's-eye view of a night city drawn like a map: thin glowing delivery routes run from hundreds of tiny restaurants and all converge into one narrow gate in the center. A giant hand reaches in from across the ocean at the top edge of the frame and takes hold of the gate, a faint red suspension bridge silhouette far away on the other shore.

An empty plot of land at dawn with surveying stakes and string lines; in the foreground a table with an unrolled blueprint of a data center building, a pencil and a coffee cup; high-voltage power lines stretch across the distant hills.
